blind_spots.blind_spot: SPU-001 is packaged and specified for a consumer reliability envelope, and nothing in their spec sheet addresses what a fielded payload does to a part
blind_spots.operator_reality: A wafer-level chip-scale package is one of the worst choices for thermal cycling, vibration and mechanical shock — the daily life of a man-worn, airborne or vehicle-mounted ISR payload. A program office asks for operating temperature range, screening level, moisture-sensitivity level, a qualification report, and a lifetime-buy/obsolescence plan before it will design a 22nm startup part into anything. None of that exists in their published specification, and generating it is a multi-quarter, capital-consuming exercise that a consumer-electronics roadmap never budgets for.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The design center and every named partner — ABOV, NewSound hearing care, the Tympan platform — is consumer electronics, where commercial-grade parts and a CES demo are the whole qualification story.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: AI Co-Processor — WLCSP for circuit integration. Specifications: 1 MB of on-chip SRAM (10 MB effective with sparsity), 22nm process, Sub-mW for speech, audio, and 1-D data, SPI interface

blind_spots.blind_spot: The ISR claim in the SBIR record rests on a hearing-aid evaluation kit; the RF front end is the part that isn't built
blind_spots.operator_reality: Their published evaluation path is EVK2 = 'EVB + Tympan open source hearing aid platform' with two MEMS microphones and a 3.5mm jack — kilohertz audio. 'Sparse AI for ISR communications' means wideband RF: gigasample-per-second digitizers, dynamic range across co-site interference, and a data path that feeds the accelerator faster than an SPI interface can move bytes. SPI is the tell — it caps ingest at a rate that makes real RF work impossible, so the demo that wins the Phase II can't be the architecture that fields.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Sparsity and sub-milliwatt inference genuinely solve the audio keyword problem, so the same story was carried into an ISR abstract without re-deriving the interface budget for the actual signal.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Evaluation Kit 2 (EVK2): EVB + Tympan open source hearing aid platform and Tympan connector board ... 2x onboard MEMS microphones, 3.5mm audio jacks for input/output

blind_spots.blind_spot: As a component vendor they need a prime to design them in, and there is no visible advocacy chain, export posture, or supply-chain story to make that possible
blind_spots.operator_reality: A chip never gets fielded on its own — it gets fielded inside a prime's box, two years after a systems engineer chose it. That decision requires an export-control determination (semiconductors and their design data are export-controlled), DFARS country-of-origin and trusted-supplier flowdowns naming the fab and the packaging house, and a government champion willing to accept single-source risk from a 22-person company. femto.ai names none of its supply chain, and the company's public energy is going to consumer OEM design wins where the sales cycle rewards a CES booth instead.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The Series A thesis (hearing aids, earbuds, security cameras, per Business Wire) pointed at consumer volume; the SBIR is a side channel, so nobody owns the design-in path on the defense side.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: femtoAI and ABOV Deliver Ultra-Efficient Edge AI For Consumer Electronics

opener_hook: Femtosense carries CAGE code 86QM8 and an SBIR portfolio entry for low-power sparse AI in ISR communications, and the evaluation path published on femto.ai is EVK2 — the SPU board bolted to the Tympan open-source hearing-aid platform with two MEMS microphones and a 3.5mm jack. Those two facts describe different products, and the SPI interface on SPU-001 is where that gap becomes an architecture problem rather than a marketing one.
what_they_do: Fabless startup selling a sub-milliwatt sparse-AI accelerator chip (SPU-001) plus SDK for on-device inference, marketed almost entirely to consumer electronics.
